questions.statement: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly?
questions.context: Present perfect with experiences, San Juan, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Correct. 'Has visited' is present perfect, and the sentence does not say when the trip happened, only that it has happened.
Incorrect. The past simple sounds fine, but the unit calls for the present perfect for an experience with no specific date.
Incorrect. After 'has' the verb goes in the past participle, and the participle of 'visit' is 'visited'.
Incorrect. The present continuous does not combine with a place, and the main verb would also be wrongly conjugated.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfecto se forma con 'have' o 'has' mas el participio pasado. Se usa para hablar de experiencias de vida sin especificar el momento, y esa ausencia de fecha es justamente lo que lo distingue del pasado simple.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'They ____ (not / decide) the destination yet.'
questions.context: Present perfect spelling rules, Ponce, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Incorrect. After 'haven't' the verb goes in the past participle, not in its base form 'decide'.
Incorrect. The past simple negative uses 'didn't' with the base form 'decide', not with the participle 'decided' used here.
Correct. The present perfect negative is 'have not' or 'haven't' plus the past participle 'decided'.
Incorrect. 'Don't' belongs to the present simple and cannot be followed by a past participle.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfecto tiene una sola negacion posible: 'have not' o 'haven't' seguido del participio. Cualquier combinacion con 'did' o 'do' corresponde a otros tiempos verbales y produce una frase que un hablante nativo no diria.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'I ____ (write) three emails to the coordinator.'
questions.context: Present perfect with irregular participles, Carolina, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Wrote' is the past simple and cannot be used as a participle after 'have'.
Correct. The participle of 'to write' is 'written', which is irregular and different from the past simple form 'wrote'.
Incorrect. Adding -ed to an irregular verb is not valid English, so the correct form is 'written'.
Incorrect. 'Am' belongs to the present continuous and does not combine with the past simple 'wrote' as the main verb.

questions.explanation:
Muchos verbos irregulares tienen un participio distinto tanto del presente como del pasado simple. 'To write' da 'wrote' en pasado y 'written' en participio, y con 'to see' ocurre lo mismo: 'saw' y 'seen'. La confusion entre estas dos formas es el error mas comun de la unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct?
questions.context: Present perfect with ever and never, Bayamon, grado 11, W05.

options.text: Did you ever ate roasted pig on the beach?
options.feedback: Incorrect. After 'did' the verb goes in the base form, so 'ate' does not belong and the sentence is incorrect.

options.text: Have you ever eat roasted pig on the beach?
options.feedback: Incorrect. The present perfect requires the participle 'eaten', not the base form 'eat'.

options.text: Do you ever ate roasted pig on the beach?
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Do' is the present simple auxiliary and cannot be followed by the past form 'ate'.

options.text: Have you ever eaten roasted pig on the beach?
options.feedback: Correct. 'Ever' goes between the auxiliary and the participle to ask about a life experience.

questions.explanation:
Los adverbios 'ever' y 'never' en presente perfecto ocupan la posicion intermedia: auxiliar, adverbio y participio. Al aparecer 'ever', la frase suele llevar una pregunta, porque se trata de preguntar por una experiencia en toda la vida.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why can't you say 'I have seen the movie yesterday'?
questions.context: Present perfect versus past simple, Arecibo, grado 11, W05.

options.text: 'Yesterday' is a plural word, so the verb needs the -s of the third person.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Yesterday' is a time adverb and has nothing to do with verb agreement.

options.text: The present perfect always requires the past simple in the second half of the sentence.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The two forms cannot be mixed in the same sentence when one of them requires a specific finished time.

options.text: 'Seen' is not the correct participle of the verb 'to see'.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Seen' is the correct participle; the problem is the time expression 'yesterday'.

options.text: 'Yesterday' is a finished past time, so the present perfect cannot be used with it.
options.feedback: Correct. The past simple requires a specific finished time, while the present perfect can only refer to the past without saying when.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfecto y el pasado simple no pueden convivir con las mismas expresiones de tiempo. Con 'yesterday', 'last year' o 'in 2019' se usa el pasado simple. Con 'already', 'yet', 'ever' o 'never' se usa el presente perfecto.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'She ____ (just / finish) her project.'
questions.context: Present perfect with just, Humacao, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The main verb must be in the past participle, so 'finish' is missing the -ed.
Correct. 'Just' goes between the auxiliary and the participle and shows that the action finished very recently.
Incorrect. The adverb goes in mid-position, after the auxiliary, not at the beginning of the sentence.
Incorrect. The order is auxiliary, adverb, participle; putting 'just' at the end breaks the present perfect structure.

questions.explanation:
Los adverbios de presente perfecto como 'just', 'already', 'still' y 'ever' van siempre entre el auxiliar y el participio. El orden 'auxiliar, adverbio, participio' es la estructura fija de este tiempo verbal.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'We ____ (wait) for the results for an hour.'
questions.context: Present perfect with regular participles, Aguadilla, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Correct. 'Have waited' is present perfect, and 'for' with a duration is compatible with this tense.
Incorrect. That gerund belongs to the present perfect continuous, which is a different unit with a different emphasis.
Incorrect. 'Had' is the past perfect, which places the waiting at a point before another past event.
Incorrect. The present continuous is used with ongoing durations, but here the sentence reports a result that is already complete.

questions.explanation:
Con 'for' y 'since' el presente perfecto es valido, y con duraciones que ya terminan tambien lo es. Lo que no es valido es mezclar el tiempo: usar 'had waited' llevaria la accion a un pasado mas remoto del que pide la frase.

questions.statement: Choose the correct tag: 'You have already eaten, ____?'
questions.context: Present perfect with question tags, Guayanilla, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Didn't' belongs to the past simple and does not fit the present perfect structure.
Incorrect. A positive statement requires a negative tag, so the 'not' in the tag is unnecessary.
Correct. A positive statement takes a negative tag, and the auxiliary 'have' is kept with the subject 'you'.
Incorrect. 'Don't' is the present simple auxiliary, not the present perfect one.

questions.explanation:
El tag del presente perfecto usa el mismo 'have' de la frase principal, con la forma contracta 'not' si la frase es positiva. La estructura es 'have you', 'have they' o 'has she' segun el sujeto, seguida de 'not' cuando corresponde.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'She has lived in Ponce ____ she was a child.'
questions.context: Present perfect with since and for, Trujillo Alto, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'For' measures a duration, and 'was a child' is a point in time, not a measurable period.
Incorrect. 'During' is used with specific periods such as 'during 2020' or 'during the summer'.
Correct. 'Since' introduces a starting point in time, and 'was a child' is a specific moment that works as that point.
Incorrect. 'From' indicates an origin or starting point, but it does not combine with the present perfect the way 'since' does.

questions.explanation:
La diferencia entre 'since' y 'for' es uno de los puntos que mas se confunden. 'Since' marca el inicio con un punto, como 'since 2019' o 'since she was a child'. 'For' marca una duracion, como 'for three years' o 'for an hour'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct question: '____ you ever been to Vieques?'
questions.context: Present perfect questions, Barceloneta, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Correct. The auxiliary 'have' opens the present perfect question, and the verb goes in the participle, which is 'been'.
Incorrect. 'Do' forms present simple questions and does not combine with 'been', which is a participle.
Incorrect. 'Did' belongs to the past simple and would require the base form 'be' after the auxiliary.
Incorrect. 'Are' opens a question with 'to be' in the present, not a present perfect question, which requires 'been'.

questions.explanation:
En las preguntas de presente perfecto el auxiliar 'have' o 'has' va al principio y el verbo principal aparece en participio pasado. Cuando ese participio es 'been', el auxiliar debe ser 'have' y nunca 'do', 'did' o 'are'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is NOT correct?
questions.context: Present perfect with specific times, Maunabo, grado 11, W05.

options.text: I have finished my homework already.
options.feedback: This sentence is correct, because 'already' is a present perfect marker.

options.text: I have finished my homework at nine o'clock.
options.feedback: Incorrect. An exact time also marks a finished past, so the sentence should use 'finished' in the past simple.

options.text: I have just finished my homework.
options.feedback: This sentence is correct, because 'just' is typical of the present perfect.

options.text: I have finished my homework last night.
options.feedback: Correct. This is the incorrect sentence: 'last night' is a finished past time and requires the past simple.

questions.explanation:
La regla general es que el presente perfecto no puede usarse con un tiempo pasado ya cerrado. Expresiones como 'last night', 'at nine o'clock' o 'in 2019' indican un momento definido y obligan al pasado simple.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'He ____ (never / be) to El Yunque before.'
questions.context: Present perfect with the verb to go, Yauco, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The auxiliary is followed by the participle 'been', not the base form 'be'.
Correct. The participle of 'to be' is 'been', and with 'he' the auxiliary is 'has', followed by 'never'.
Incorrect. 'Have' agrees with I, you, we and they, and the subject of the sentence is 'he', in the third person.
Incorrect. 'Was' is the past simple of 'to be' and is not the present perfect auxiliary.

questions.explanation:
'To be' es uno de los verbos que mas se confunden en presente perfecto. El participio es 'been', y la frase necesita un 'have' o 'has' delante. Un pasado de 'to be' como 'was' pertenece a otra unidad temporal.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The teacher ____ (give) us extra homework.'
questions.context: Present perfect with third person, Cayey, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Gave' is the past simple and does not work as a participle after 'has'.
Correct. The irregular participle of 'to give' is 'given', and with 'the teacher' the auxiliary is 'has'.
Incorrect. 'Have' does not agree with the third-person singular subject 'the teacher'.
Incorrect. 'Gived' does not exist in English, because 'to give' is a fully irregular verb.

questions.explanation:
Los verbos dar, ver y hacer tienen participios que cambian por completo la raiz. 'To give' da 'gave' y 'given', 'to see' da 'saw' y 'seen', y 'to do' da 'did' y 'done'. El participio es la forma que exige el presente perfecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Question: 'Have you submitted the form?' Answer: '____'
questions.context: Present perfect in short answers, San Sebastian, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Did' answers a past simple question, not one formed with 'have'.
Incorrect. It is a valid answer but not a short one; the short form leaves out the participle.
Incorrect. 'Submitted' is past simple and does not match the question with the auxiliary 'have'.
Correct. The short answer repeats the auxiliary 'have' from the question, which is the expected form.

questions.explanation:
Las respuestas cortas siguen el auxiliar de la pregunta. Si la pregunta abre con 'have' o 'has', la respuesta abre igual, y si abre con 'did' la respuesta usa 'did'. Ese unico criterio decide entre 'have', 'has' y 'did'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the prepositions correctly?
questions.context: Present perfect with for versus since, Camuy, grado 11, W05.

options.text: He has worked at the hospital since five years.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Since' is not used with a period of time: it needs a starting point, such as 'since 2019'.

options.text: He has worked at the hospital for 2019.
options.feedback: Incorrect. A year is a starting point, not a duration, so the correct preposition would be 'since'.

options.text: He has worked at the hospital for five years.
options.feedback: Correct. 'For' measures duration and is followed by a period of time, such as 'five years' or 'two months'.

options.text: He has worked at the hospital since five years ago.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Since five years ago' mixes a point in time with a duration; the natural English structure is 'for five years'.

questions.explanation:
La preposicion depende de lo que sigue. Si lo que sigue es una cantidad de tiempo se usa 'for'; si es una fecha, una hora o un evento se usa 'since'. La combinacion 'since five years ago' es la que mas errores produce en los exámenes.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does this sentence express? 'He has lived in Mayaguez since 2019.'
questions.context: Present perfect with ongoing situations, Luquillo, grado 11, W05.

options.text: A situation that started in the past and is still true now.
options.feedback: Correct. The present perfect with 'since' describes a situation that began in the past and continues into the present.

options.text: A completed action with a specific date.
options.feedback: Incorrect. With a finished date, the present perfect would be replaced by the past simple, as in 'He lived there in 2019'.

options.text: A future plan that has been decided.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The present perfect with 'since' does not express future plans; it describes a situation that has already started and is still true now.

options.text: A habitual action that happened repeatedly.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Habitual actions are expressed with the present simple, not with 'has lived'.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfecto tiene dos usos principales: experiences sin fecha y situaciones que empiezan en el pasado y siguen ahora. Con 'since' se expresa siempre la segunda, y esa es la clave para elegir el tiempo verbal en esta unidad.

questions.statement: Choose the correct form: 'I ____ (not / finish) the assignment yet.'
questions.context: Present perfect negatives with yet, Toa Baja, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Correct. 'Yet' goes at the end of the sentence and fits the present perfect negative to show that something has not happened.
Incorrect. It mixes the past simple with the participle, and 'yet' also calls for the present perfect.
Incorrect. 'Don't' is present simple and cannot be followed by the participle 'finished'.
Incorrect. After the auxiliary you need the past participle 'finished', not the base form 'finish'.

questions.explanation:
La palabra 'yet' solo se usa con presente perfecto, y suele ir al final de la oracion. En preguntas se traduce como 'ya' y en frases negativas como 'todavia no', pero gramaticalmente siempre acompaña a 'have' o 'has'.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: '____ you ever seen the shark tank in Aguadilla?'
questions.context: Present perfect with the verb to see, Naguabo, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Did' belongs to the past simple and would require the base form 'see' after the auxiliary.
Incorrect. 'Do' forms the present simple and does not combine with the participle 'seen'.
Incorrect. 'Has' is for the third person singular, and the subject of the question is 'you'.
Correct. With 'you' the auxiliary is 'have', and the irregular participle of 'to see' is 'seen'.

questions.explanation:
En el presente perfecto la concordancia del auxiliar depende del sujeto: 'have' para I, you, we y they, y 'has' para he, she e it. El participio es la misma forma para todos, y por eso 'seen' no cambia de forma.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'Maria ____ (buy) the ticket online last week.'
questions.context: Present perfect with third person, Hatillo, grado 11, W05.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Buyed' does not exist in English; the present perfect requires the irregular participle 'bought', not a form made with -ed.
Correct. 'Last week' refers to a finished past, so it takes the irregular past simple 'bought', not the present perfect.
Incorrect. 'Buyed' does not exist in English, because 'to buy' is irregular and its past form is 'bought'.
Incorrect. You do not add -ed to an irregular verb; 'bought' is already the complete past simple form.

questions.explanation:

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses 'since' with the right time expression?
questions.context: Present perfect with prepositions of time, Yabucoa, grado 11, W05.

options.text: I haven't seen him since Monday ago.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Ago' does not combine with 'since', because 'since Monday' already sets the starting point.

options.text: I didn't see him since Monday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Since' requires the present perfect; with 'did', the sentence would need 'until' or a finished time reference.

options.text: I haven't seen him since Monday.
options.feedback: Correct. 'Since' with a specific day marks the starting point, so it calls for the present perfect.

options.text: I haven't see him since Monday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. After 'haven't' the verb takes the participle, so 'see' must be 'seen'.

questions.explanation:
Las preposiciones de tiempo condicionan el tiempo verbal. 'Since' y 'for' obligan al presente perfecto, mientras que 'ago' y las fechas cerradas obligan al pasado simple. Mezclarlas, como en 'since Monday ago', produce una frase que no existe en ingles.
